one_line_value_proposition: Physiotherapist-guided digital osteoarthritis programme with NICE HTG766 and NG226 recommendations — structured exercise and education for hip and knee OA at scale.
why_it_matters_locally: MSK conditions are the largest single cause of disability and a major driver of GP and orthopaedic demand. Joint Academy provides a physiotherapist-guided digital programme for hip and knee OA patients, reducing pressure on face-to-face physiotherapy services and orthopaedic waiting lists.
target_problem_statement: Long orthopaedic waiting lists, limited physiotherapy capacity, and inadequate structured support for osteoarthritis self-management between appointments.
evidence_summary: NICE HTG766 recommendation based on multiple RCTs. Shukla et al. (2022) RCT (n=211): 49% achieved clinically meaningful pain improvement vs 27% in usual care. Real-world registry (n=50,000+): 69% clinically meaningful improvement in joint pain at 12 weeks. Nero et al. (2020) RCT: reduced physiotherapy visits by 50% with non-inferior outcomes.
evidence_strength_rationale: Multiple RCTs, large real-world registry, and NICE HTG recommendation. Evidence aligns to Servita scoring for 'strong' — randomised evidence in relevant population with meaningful outcomes.

clinical_evidence_detailed.ref: Shukla et al. (2022) — Digital OA treatment RCT
clinical_evidence_detailed.outcome: 49% of digital treatment group achieved clinically meaningful pain improvement vs 27% in usual care at 12 weeks (NNT=4.5)

clinical_evidence_detailed.ref: Nero et al. (2020) — Non-inferiority RCT vs face-to-face physio
clinical_evidence_detailed.outcome: Digital treatment non-inferior to face-to-face physiotherapy for pain and function. 50% fewer clinic visits needed.
69% of patients achieved clinically meaningful improvement in joint pain at 12 weeks across international deployments.

clinical_evidence_detailed.ref: Dahlberg et al. (2020) — Healthcare utilisation study
clinical_evidence_detailed.outcome: Patients using digital OA programme had 40% fewer physiotherapy visits and 30% fewer orthopaedic consultations over 12 months.

case_studies.title: NHS MSK Pathway Redesign — South East
case_studies.outcome: Deployment across 850 patients per year with 34% reduction in referrals to secondary care orthopaedics. Average wait to treatment reduced from 12 weeks to 48 hours.

case_studies.title: First Contact Practitioner Integration
case_studies.outcome: 420 patients referred via FCP route. 71% completed 12-week programme. GP follow-up appointments reduced by 2.3 visits per patient per year.

target_patients: Adults with mild to moderate hip or knee osteoarthritis suitable for conservative management.
exclusions: Not indicated for patients requiring urgent surgical intervention or those with contraindications to exercise.
onboarding_detail: Clinician or physiotherapist referral. Patient accesses app-based programme with assigned physiotherapist guidance.
supplier_wrap: Joint Academy provides physiotherapist support, digital programme and outcome reporting.
local_wraparound_detail: Low local effort. Referral pathway required. Analytics dashboard available for population monitoring.
training_note: Minimal training required for referring clinicians.
monitoring_model: Guided self-help with physiotherapist oversight. Not continuously monitored.
monitoring_note: Guided self-help with physiotherapist check-ins. Not a continuously monitored clinical service.
escalation_note: Escalation to clinical services as clinically indicated. Programme includes safety screening.
indicative_price_text: Pricing is per patient pathway (typically 12 weeks of active treatment with maintenance access). Indicative cost per patient is in the range of £200–£350 depending on volume commitments. Commissioners should request a formal pricing proposal.
service_wrap_description: Full clinical service wrap included: dedicated physiotherapist per patient, personalised exercise programme, patient education, in-app progress monitoring, and commissioner outcome reporting. No additional clinical staffing required from the commissioner.
service_wrap_note: Physiotherapist support and analytics included in per-patient fee.
contract_note: Contact Joint Academy for NHS procurement options.
procurement_notes: Not currently available on a national NHS framework. Local procurement required via direct award or competitive process. Several AHSN regions have facilitated introductions and supported procurement. Supplier has experience with NHS standard contract terms.
expected_benefit_note: International evidence suggests 30–40% of OA patients completing the programme may achieve sufficient symptom improvement to defer or avoid joint replacement surgery. Each deferred hip or knee replacement represents approximately £6,000–£8,000 in direct surgical costs plus rehabilitation.
tariff_considerations: Joint replacement is a high-value tariff activity. Reductions in surgical volumes may have significant financial implications for orthopaedic provider trusts. Model using orthopaedic outpatient and physiotherapy costs and align incentives in pathway redesign.
provider_income_note: Orthopaedic providers should be engaged early. A reduction in surgical referrals may impact provider income from elective orthopaedic tariffs. Consider joint commissioning approaches that share benefits between commissioner and provider.
roi_note: If 30% of referred patients defer surgery, net savings can be substantial at indicative programme cost of ~£250 per patient versus £6,000–£8,000 surgical cost avoidance per deferred procedure. UK-specific ROI data is still developing.
minimum_conditions_for_success: Referral pathway with MSK first-contact practitioners or GPs. Minimum 200 patient cohort for meaningful outcome data.
demo_notes: Contact Joint Academy for a demonstration.
source_summary: NICE HTG766, NICE NG226, Joint Academy website.
confidence_note: Content based on publicly available information. Verify current assurance, pricing and data residency with Joint Academy before procurement.
